article_title: PostgreSQL 19 Beta 4 Reverts Six Features, Including Property Graph Queries, as Project Targets an October Release

content_preview.title: PostgreSQL 19 Beta 4 Reverts Six Features, Including Property Graph Queries, as Project Targets an October Release
content_preview.summary: PostgreSQL 19 Beta 4, released September 24, reverts SQL/PGQ graph queries, online checksum toggling, and four other features as the project targets an October general availability.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

The PostgreSQL Global Development Group released the fourth beta of PostgreSQL 19 on September 24, 2026, pulling six previously announced features out of the release just weeks before its planned general availability, [according to the project's announcement](https://www.postgresql.org/about/news/postgresql-19-beta-4-released-3386/). editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Verified all six reverted-feature claims verbatim against source-0's 'Changes Since Beta 3' list: (1) 'Revert SQL/PGQ (property graph query) support.' — matches article. (2) 'Revert online enabling and disabling of data checksums.' — matches. (3) 'Revert support for temporal updates/deletes provided by the FOR PORTION OF clause.' — matches. (4) 'Revert ALTER TABLE ... MERGE PARTITIONS and ALTER TABLE ... SPLIT PARTITIONS.' — matches. (5) 'Remove the pg_get_role_ddl(), pg_get_tablespace_ddl(), and pg_get_database_ddl() functions.' — matches. (6) 'Revert a change that forced LC_COLLATE to C in the postmaster process.' — matches. All other quoted material (REPACK fixes, WAIT FOR fixes, FOREIGN_JOIN/pg_plan_advice fix, CREATE PUBLICATION ... EXCEPT fixes, logical replication sync fix, autovacuum scoring fixes, COPY FROM SIMD fix, partition-detach crash fix, pgbench --continue-on-error clarification, RC/GA timing quote, beta-caution quote) is verbatim from source-0. Backstory cross-references verified: Beta 1 shipped 2026-06-04 per source-1 ('Posted on 2026-06-04') — matches article's 'June 4, 2026'; source-1 confirms SQL/PGQ, FOR PORTION OF UPDATE/DELETE support, ALTER TABLE MERGE/SPLIT PARTITIONS, and online data-checksum toggling were all part of Beta 1's original feature set, matching the article's framing. Beta 3 shipped 2026-08-13 per source-2 ('Posted on 2026-08-13') — matches article's 'August 13'; source-2 contains both 'Revert GROUP BY ALL.' and 'Several fixes for the new FOR PORTION OF temporal table syntax.' verbatim, exactly as quoted in the article. Both internal cross-reference links (/article/2026-06/05-postgresql-19-beta-1-... and /article/2026-08/25-postgresql-ships-coordinated-release-...) resolve to real, already-published articles in src/content/articles/, and those articles' own frontmatter (dates, source URLs, feature descriptions) is consistent with the new article's backstory claims. No hallucinated quotes or fabricated specifics found.
